title: Breakfast on the beach (John 21:1–19)
hookLine: a charcoal fire, fish, and three times, do you love me
carry: thou knowest that I love thee

cards: Galilee, back where it all began. Peter does what he knows. In the Douay-Rheims: "I go a fishing."
Six others go with him. They fish all night and catch nothing. At dawn a man on the shore calls out: children, have you caught anything?
No. Throw the net on the right side of the boat. They do, and the net is so full they can't haul it in.
The beloved disciple looks at the shore: it is the Lord. And Peter, who can't wait for the boat, throws on his coat and jumps into the sea.

teach.b: On the beach, Jesus already has a fire going, with fish on it and bread. Come and dine, he says. Here's a detail you'd miss in English.
John uses the same Greek word for this charcoal fire as for the fire in the high priest's courtyard, where Peter stood warming himself and denied him three times. Same smell of smoke.
After breakfast, Jesus turns to Peter. "Simon son of John, lovest thou me more than these?" Peter says: "Yea, Lord, thou knowest that I love thee."
Feed my lambs. He asks a second time: same answer, same charge. Then a third time, and John says Peter was grieved, because he asked him the third time.

teach.h: DO YOU LOVE ME? THREE TIMES.
teach.b: He'd said I don't know him three times; now he's asked do you love me three times. He answers with everything he has: "Lord, thou knowest all things: thou knowest that I love thee." Jesus doesn't make him grovel.
Each answer comes back with a job: feed my sheep.
And by the same lake where he first called Peter after another night of empty nets, two words: follow me.

teach.h: THOU KNOWEST THAT I LOVE THEE.
teach.b: Catholics read this as Jesus giving Peter the care of his whole flock, part of why they see Peter, and the popes after him, as shepherd of the Church.
Then they walk along the shore, Peter beside him, and the beloved disciple following behind.

how: Catholics hear this Gospel in the Easter season and read it, with Matthew 16, as part of Peter's commission to shepherd the Church, a role they see continued in the pope.

o: a fire lit for a sacrifice at the temple
a signal fire guiding the boats to shore
a fire like the one at Peter's denial

games.q: what's inside the breakfast — tap the pairs.
p: the right side of the boat
where the full net came up
the beloved disciple, first to see
the courtyard, and now the beach
the job that came with each answer

s: Jesus reminds Peter of his three denials
he never mentions the courtyard. he asks three times, do you love me?
John uses the same word for the fire at Peter's denial and the fire at this breakfast
Peter waited for the boat to reach shore
he threw on his coat and jumped into the sea.

games.q: you're Peter in the boat. the beloved disciple says, it is the Lord. the shore is about two hundred cubits away. what do you do?
o: throw on your coat and jump into the sea.
games.why: he girds his coat and throws himself into the water. the man who failed him doesn't hang back. he swims.

practice: Each of Peter's answers came back as a job: feed my sheep.

Bring to mind the people who depend on you a little, at home, at work, down the street, choose one, and ask what feeding them would look like: a real meal, a message they've been waiting for, an hour of help, not a grand gesture, one plate.
If you pray, you can answer the question for yourself: do you love me?

wordCard.voice: charcoal fire. The same kind that burned at Peter's denial, now cooking breakfast for him on the beach.

orig.note: Greek: a charcoal fire. John's word for the fire at Peter's denial and at this breakfast.

carryVoice: Your line: thou knowest that I love thee. The fire that saw the failure cooked the breakfast. See you tomorrow.
